as_told.title: Dynastic Egyptians recarved the Sphinx head, too small for the body

plain: This story is about the Great Sphinx, the huge stone statue at Giza in Egypt with a lion's body and a human head. The writer Graham Hancock says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the Sphinx was first carved entirely as a lion, and that the pharaohs, Egypt's ancient kings, later recut the head. He credits the researchers Robert Schoch, John Anthony West and Manu Seyfzadeh. Matt LaCroix, another researcher, points out that the head is too small for the body, which he says shows it was recarved by later Egyptians. Michels adds that a lion would have lined up with the constellation Leo at the spring equinox around 10,500 BC. If true, the Sphinx would be far older than the pharaohs, made by an earlier, forgotten people.
